To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) students are not making cross-curricular connections in their classrooms; (2) the students in our study did not make connections to other subject areas during classroom discussion; (3) teachers did not use strategies to facilitate cross-curricular connections during classroom discussion; and (4) teachers do not use strategies to help students make cross-curricular connections when they teach integrated curricula.
The use of a cross-curricular approach can enhance student learning in both mathematics and science.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how students develop cross-curricula connections and how teachers facilitate the development of these connections.
the question of how to teach an integrated curriculum in such a way that students develop cross-curriculum connections.
the question of whether students make connections between subject matter in integrated units and, if so, what strategies can be used to promote such connections.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Brain Surfing strategy is an effective tool to facilitate cross-curricular connections in an integrated classroom.
Brain Surfing is a strategy for making cross curricular connections.
the use of Brain Surfing in a classroom can be an effective way for students to develop connections between subject areas.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we are trying to help students make cross-curricular connections, to develop a more complete understanding of the material being taught, and to become better thinkers and problem solvers by using a strategy we call Brain Surfing.

the students who participated in this study were more likely to make connections between subject area content when the teacher used the strategy Brain Surfing than they were when the teacher used a traditional discussion format.
the more students are engaged in their learning the more likely it is that they will make cross-curricular connections and develop higher-order thinking skills.
The main takeaway from our work is that
students need opportunities to make connections to their own lives, to other disciplines, and to the larger world in order to develop a sense of ownership of the content they are studying.
students need to be given the opportunity to develop their own connections to content and to make those connections explicit in their work.
we need to help our students make cross-curricular connections, and we need to help them make these connections on their own.
